# Draft:Battle of Grodek

----
The Battle of Gródek (also spelled Gorodok) was a minor engagement during World War I fought in late August 1914 near the town of Gródek in Galicia, then part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire (modern-day Ukraine). The battle involved Russian forces of the Russian Imperial Army clashing with Austro-Hungarian troops as part of the early Battle of Galicia campaign. Although a smaller engagement, the fighting at Gródek contributed to the Russian advance and the operational developments leading to larger battles in the region.
In August 1914, following the outbreak of World War I, the Russian Empire launched an offensive into Galicia, aiming to defeat Austro-Hungarian forces and secure territory along the eastern frontier. Russian troops advanced rapidly, encountering Austro-Hungarian defensive positions near key towns such as Gródek. Russian commanders sought to seize control of strategic river crossings along the San River to facilitate further operations.
During the engagement at Gródek, Russian forces attacked Austro-Hungarian positions defending the town and nearby river crossings. Combat involved infantry and artillery, with Russian troops pressing the advance against prepared defenses. Austro-Hungarian units offered resistance but were eventually forced to withdraw, allowing Russian forces to consolidate control in the area.
The Russian victory at Gródek enabled continued advances into eastern Galicia and disrupted Austro-Hungarian defensive plans. While casualties were relatively low compared to larger battles of the campaign, the engagement helped shape troop movements and set the stage for subsequent confrontations during the Battle of Galicia.
The Battle of Gródek illustrates the operational challenges of early World War I Eastern Front engagements and the role of smaller battles in influencing broader campaign outcomes. Historians cite the battle as an example of localized clashes that had strategic consequences during the Russian invasion of Galicia.
